## 48 teams. 3 host countries. 1 way to keep up.

I’ve been fortunate to cover the beautiful game in some form for 22 years. In all that time, I’ve never been more excited about an editorial project than the expansion of the Guardian’s US soccer coverage. We’ve built an expert team to uphold the Guardian’s proud tradition of unflinching journalism that speaks truth to power, while breaking new ground in deepening Americans’ love for the game.

**The best way to experience our comprehensive, independent World Cup coverage is in the Guardian app: you can follow each reporter and follow your favorite team, with live score updates and live blogs for every game as it happens.**

For as many exciting on-field moments there may be during the 2026 World Cup, there will be plenty of off-field stories to follow: about the US’s rapidly changing posture towards its co-hosts; our president’s clear desire to leverage the tournament for political aims; about the cities and communities impacted by the influx of visitors; and the financial cost at a time when affordability is a real issue for so many Americans.**I can’t recommend enough that you download the app now to stay connected to our reporting. And once you do… it’s game on.**

Alexander Abnos

Senior sports editor
